extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists and photojournalists interested in Pulitzer winners
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the Pulitzer Prize for Feature Photography: what the prize recognizes, its history, and a year-by-year list of winners with the citation/rationale for each award. Useful for understanding the types of photographic work the prize honors.

rubrics_metrics.name: What the prize recognizes
rubrics_metrics.description: "It recognizes a distinguished example of feature photography in black and white or color, which may consist of a photograph or photographs, a sequence or an album.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize may be awarded for a single photograph, a sequence/portfolio, or an album; both black-and-white and color work are eligible. The winners' citations illustrate that honored work frequently features strong human storytelling, intimate portraits, documentary photo essays, coverage of crises (war, famine, disasters), and images that convey social impact or emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarding frequency and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: "One Feature Photography Pulitzer has been awarded annually from 1968, with the exception of 1985, when two prizes were awarded.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prize is essentially annual since its 1968 inauguration; historical anomalies (e.g., two awards in 1985) are noted. The list of winners documents year-by-year recipients and their cited rationales, which reflect the board's selection in each year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category origin and relation to other photography Pulitzers
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Feature Photography prize was inaugurated in 1968 when the single Pulitzer Prize for Photography was replaced by the Feature prize and 'Pulitzer Prize for Spot News Photography' (renamed 'Pulitzer Prize for Breaking News Photography' in 2000).",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explains the category's historical scope and its separation from spot/breaking-news photography. Notes and footnotes indicate that the Pulitzer board sometimes moves entries between photography categories; many winners were moved from Spot/Breaking News Photography in earlier years.
